claim: Intracellular inclusions rich in alpha-synuclein are a hallmark of several neuropathological diseases including Parkinson's disease (PD).
source: Intracellular inclusions rich in alpha-synuclein are a hallmark of several neuropathological diseases including Parkinson's disease (PD).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by the general scientific knowledge and the context of the manuscript.

claim: A previous study reported the structure of alpha-synuclein fibrils (residues 1–121), composed of two protofibrils connected via a densely-packed interface formed by residues 50–57.
source: Previously, we reported the structure of alpha-synuclein fibrils (residues 1–121), composed of two protofibrils that are connected via a densely-packed interface formed by residues 50–57 (Guerrero-Ferreira, eLife 218;7:e36402).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous publication by the authors.

claim: Two new polymorphic atomic structures of alpha-synuclein fibrils termed polymorphs 2a and 2b were determined at 3.0 Å and 3.4 Å resolution, respectively.
source: We here report two new polymorphic atomic structures of alpha-synuclein fibrils termed polymorphs 2a and 2b, at 3.0 Å and 3.4 Å resolution, respectively.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the cryo-EM data presented in the manuscript, including resolution values from image processing.

claim: The new polymorphs 2a and 2b show a radically different structure compared to previously reported polymorphs.
source: These polymorphs show a radically different structure compared to previously reported polymorphs.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison data presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figure 4 and related discussions.

claim: The new structures have a 10 nm fibril diameter.
source: The new structures have a 10 nm fibril diameter and are composed of two protofilaments which interact via intermolecular salt-bridges between amino acids K45, E57 (polymorph 2a) or E46 (polymorph 2b).
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM measurements and structural analysis.

claim: Polymorphs 2a and 2b are composed of two protofilaments which interact via intermolecular salt-bridges between amino acids K45, E57 (polymorph 2a) or E46 (polymorph 2b).
source: The new structures have a 10 nm fibril diameter and are composed of two protofilaments which interact via intermolecular salt-bridges between amino acids K45, E57 (polymorph 2a) or E46 (polymorph 2b).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structures and atomic models.

claim: The non-amyloid component (NAC) region of alpha-synuclein is fully buried by interactions with the N-terminus in polymorphs 2a and 2b.
source: The non-amyloid component (NAC) region of alpha-synuclein is fully buried by previously non-described interactions with the N-terminus.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structures showing the N-terminal region wrapping around the NAC region.

claim: Lewy bodies (LB) and Lewy neurites (LN) are neuropathological hallmarks of Parkinson's disease and other Lewy body disorders.
source: Lewy bodies (LB) and Lewy neurites (LN) are neuropathological hallmarks of Parkinson's disease and other Lewy body disorders.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge in the field of neurodegenerative diseases.

claim: Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites contain a cytoplasmic enrichment of the protein alpha-synuclein.
source: These intracellular neuronal features contain a cytoplasmic enrichment of the protein alpha-synuclein (α-Syn), thereby defining these diseases as synucleinopathies (Spillantini et al., 1998a; Spillantini et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: Certain mutations in the α-Syn gene (SNCA) cause familial forms of PD and other synucleinopathies.
source: Apart from this finding in the postmortem brain, the central role of α-Syn in Parkinson's disease (PD) is highlighted by the fact that certain mutations in the α-Syn gene (SNCA) cause familial forms of PD and other synucleinopathies (Appel-Cresswell et al., 2013; Krüger et al., 1998; Lesage et al., 2013; Pasanen et al., 2014; Polymeropoulos et al., 1997; Zarranz et al., 2004)
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited research publications.

claim: Duplication or triplication of the SNCA gene lead to either a sporadic or early-onset PD, respectively, in affected families.
source: and that duplication or triplication of the SNCA gene lead to either a sporadic or early-onset PD, respectively, in affected families (Chartier-Harlin et al., 2004; Flagmeier et al., 2016; Fujioka et al., 2014; Ibáñez et al., 2004; Singleton et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited research publications.

claim: The 14 kDa protein α-Syn is known to readily form fibrils in vitro.
source: The 14 kDa protein α-Syn is known to readily form fibrils in vitro (Conway et al., 1998; Hashimoto et al., 1998)
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: α-Syn fibrils induce α-Syn inclusions when injected in model animals.
source: and induce α-Syn inclusions when injected in model animals (Mougenot et al., 2012; Peelaerts et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: A slight minority of analyzed LBs contained filamentous or dense proteinaceous structures, while the vast majority of LBs was primarily composed of membrane fragments.
source: They found that a slight minority of analyzed LBs contained filamentous or dense proteinaceous structures, while the vast majority of LBs was primarily composed of membrane fragments (Lewis et al., 2019; Shahmoradian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications using correlative imaging by electron microscopy.

claim: α-Syn protein consists of 140 amino acids.
source: α-Syn protein consists of 140 amino acids.
evidence: This is a basic structural fact about the protein.

claim: The N-terminus (residues 1–60) is rich in lysine residues and contains KTK lipid-binding motif repeats associated with vesicle binding.
source: The N-terminus (residues 1–60) is rich in lysine residues and contains KTK lipid-binding motif repeats associated with vesicle binding (George, 2002; George et al., 1995; Perrin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: The N-terminus contains all known SNCA familial PD mutations: A30P, E46K, H50Q, G51D, A53E, and A53T.
source: It is also the region which contains all known SNCA familial PD mutations: A30P (Krüger et al., 1998), E46K (Zarranz et al., 2004), H50Q (Appel-Cresswell et al., 2013; Proukakis et al., 2013), G51D (Lesage et al., 2013), A53E (Pasanen et al., 2014), and A53T (Polymeropoulos et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited research publications.

claim: The central region (residues 61–95) is the non-amyloid-ß component (NAC region).
source: The central region (residues 61–95) is the non-amyloid-ß component (NAC region) (Giasson et al., 2001; Uéda et al., 1993)
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: The NAC region is essential for α-Syn aggregation.
source: which is essential for α-Syn aggregation (Li et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a cited research publication.

claim: ß-synuclein lacks a stretch of 12 aminoacid residues within the NAC region (residues 71–82) and is unable to form fibrils.
source: The related protein ß-synuclein (ß-syn) (Jakes et al., 1994; Stefanis, 2012) lacks a stretch of 12 aminoacid residues within the NAC region (residues 71–82) and is unable to form fibrils.
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: The highly unstructured C-terminus of α-Syn (residues 96–140) can bind calcium and is populated by negatively charged residues.
source: The highly unstructured C-terminus of α-Syn (residues 96–140) can bind calcium and it is populated by negatively charged residues (Li et al., 2007; Post et al., 2018; Vilar et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: Truncation of the C-terminal domain may play a role in α-Syn pathology by promoting fibril formation.
source: Truncation of this domain may play a role in α-Syn pathology by promoting fibril formation (Crowther et al., 1998; Li et al., 2005; Liu et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: C-terminal truncation is involved in Lewy body formation.
source: and being involved in Lewy body formation (Dufty et al., 2007; Mahul-Mellier et al., 2019; Prasad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited research publications.

claim: Inhibition of C-terminal truncation has been shown to reduce neurodegeneration in a transgenic mouse model of Multiple System Atrophy (MSA).
source: Inhibition of C-terminal truncation has also been shown to reduce neurodegeneration in a transgenic mouse model of Multiple System Atrophy (MSA) (Bassil et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a cited research publication.

claim: Helical image processing of 100'323 fibril segments extracted from 1'143 micrographs revealed the presence of two distinct fibril polymorphs at the step of 3D classification.
source: Helical image processing of 100'323 fibril segments extracted from 1'143 micrographs, revealed the presence of two distinct fibril polymorphs at the step of 3D classification.
evidence: This is directly supported by the cryo-EM data processing described in the manuscript.

claim: The left-twisting handedness of the fibrils was confirmed by AFM imaging.
source: The left-twisting handedness of the fibrils was confirmed by AFM imaging, as done previously (Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by AFM data and a citation to previous work.

claim: The maps show clear side-chain densities and ß-strand separation along the helical axis.
source: The maps show clear side-chain densities and ß-strand separation along the helical axis
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM density maps.

claim: Both fibril types are formed by two protofilaments of approximately 5 nm diameter, which are composed of distinct rungs of density.
source: and indicate that both fibril types are formed by two protofilaments of approximately 5 nm diameter, which are composed of distinct rungs of density.
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structures.

claim: For each protofilament of α-Syn polymorph 2a, successive rungs of ß-strands are related by helical symmetry with a rise of 4.8 Å and a twist of −0.80°.
source: In each protofilament of the new α-Syn polymorph 2a, successive rungs of ß-strands are related by helical symmetry with a rise of 4.8 Å and a twist of −0.80°
evidence: This is determined from the cryo-EM helical reconstruction parameters.

claim: The subunits within the two protofilaments of polymorph 2a are packed in the same plane, facing each other in two-fold symmetry.
source: with the subunits within the two protofilaments packed in the same plane, facing each other (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) in two-fold symmetry.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and illustrated in the figures.

claim: The two protofilaments in α-Syn polymorph 2b are offset by 2.4 Å in height between each other, related by an approximate 21 screw symmetry with a twist of 179.55°.
source: Distinctively, the two protofilaments in α-Syn polymorph 2b are offset by 2.4 Å in height between each other, related by an approximate 21 screw symmetry with a twist of 179.55° (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is determined from the cryo-EM helical reconstruction parameters and illustrated in the figures.

claim: In α-Syn polymorph 2a, residue K45 of one protofilament forms a salt-bridge with residue E57 of the other protofilament, and vice-versa.
source: In α-Syn polymorph 2a, residue K45 of one protofilament forms a salt-bridge with residue E57 of the other protofilament, and vice-versa (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the atomic model built from the cryo-EM density.

claim: In α-Syn polymorph 2b, the interaction between protofilaments occurs only through salt-bridges between residues K45 and E46 from adjacent protofilaments.
source: In α-Syn polymorph 2b, the interaction between protofilaments occurs only through salt-bridges between residues K45 and E46 from adjacent protofilaments (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the atomic model built from the cryo-EM density.

claim: For polymorph 2a and polymorph 2b, each α-Syn molecule within a protofilament is composed of eight in-register parallel ß-strands (ß0–7): residues 16–20 (ß0), 38–44 (ß1), 46–50 (ß2), 52–56 (ß3), 61–66 (ß4), 68–72 (ß5), 76–79 (ß6), and 85–92 (ß7).
source: For polymorph 2a (PDB ID 6SSX) and polymorph 2b (PDB ID 6SST), each α-Syn molecule within a protofilament is composed of eight in-register parallel ß-strands (ß0–7; Figure 1A,D and E): residues 16–20 (ß0), 38–44 (ß1), 46–50 (ß2), 52–56 (ß3), 61–66 (ß4), 68–72 (ß5), 76–79 (ß6), and 85–92 (ß7).
evidence: This is determined from the atomic models built from the cryo-EM densities.

claim: The NAC region encompasses ß-strands ß4 to ß7 and appears entirely surrounded by densities in the cryo-EM map.
source: The NAC region encompasses ß-strands ß4 to ß7 and it appears entirely surrounded by densities in our cryo-EM map with ß1 to ß3 on one side of the fibril and additional densities on the other side.
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM density maps.

claim: Minor differences between polymorphs 2a and 2b are observed in the turn between ß3 and ß4.
source: Minor differences between polymorphs 2a and 2b are observed in the turn between ß3 and ß4 (Figure 1D and E, Figure 2A and C).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the atomic models of the two polymorphs.

claim: There are considerable changes in the height of the α-Syn monomer along the helical axis, with the highest point being ß3 and the lowest ß4.
source: As described for α-Syn polymorph 1a (Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2018), and also shown in patient-derived Tau filaments (Fitzpatrick et al., 2017), there are considerable changes in the height of the α-Syn monomer along the helical axis, with the highest point being ß3 and the lowest ß4 (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structures and supported by citations to similar observations in other amyloid structures.

claim: In polymorphs 2a and 2b, two bent β-arches orient back-to-back, one showing a single, and the other showing two bends.
source: However, the components and the orientation of ß-strands contributing to the motifs are now radically different. In polymorphs 2a and 2b, two bent β-arches orient back-to-back, one showing a single, and the other showing two bends.
evidence: This is observed in the atomic models of the structures.

claim: The first β-arch is formed by strands 1/6, 2/5 and 3/4, with bends located at residues K45/V74, G51/G67, and the tip formed by K58.
source: The first β-arch is formed by strands 1/6, 2/5 and 3/4, with bends located at residues K45/V74, G51/G67, and the tip formed by K58.
evidence: This is determined from the atomic models of the structures.

claim: The second bent β-arch shares β-strands 4, 5 and 6 with the first one, and comprises in addition β-strand 7.
source: The second bent β-arch shares β-strands 4, 5 and 6 with the first one, and comprises in addition β-strand 7
evidence: This is determined from the atomic models of the structures.

claim: Residue I88 marks the beginning of a hydrophobic area composed of residues A89, A90, A91, F94 and V95, which contribute to the stabilization of an additional beta-strand density.
source: Interestingly, residue I88 marks the beginning of a hydrophobic area composed of residues A89, A90, A91, F94 and V95, which contribute to the stabilization of an additional beta-strand density that is clearly visible in the cryo-EM maps of both polymorphs (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM density maps and atomic models.

claim: The interacting region in polymorph 2a corresponds to a hydrophobic stretch formed by residues V16 to E20, termed β0.
source: We propose that this interacting region corresponds in polymorph 2a to a hydrophobic stretch formed by residues V16 to E20, and here use for it the term β0.
evidence: This is proposed based on the cryo-EM density and supported by NMR data.

claim: This region was previously shown to be an isolated ß-strand identified in the N-terminus of α-Syn fibrils by solid-state NMR on equivalent fibril preparations.
source: This region was previously shown to be an isolated ß-strand identified in the N-terminus of α-Syn fibrils by solid-state NMR on equivalent fibril preparations (Bousset et al., 2013; Gath et al., 2014a) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by cited NMR studies on similar fibril preparations.

claim: The localization of the stretch can be derived from cross peaks present in NMR 2D PAR spectra that connect S87 to A17, A18 and A19.
source: The localization of the stretch can be derived from cross peaks present in NMR 2D PAR (De Paëpe et al., 2008) spectra that connect S87 to A17, A18 and A19 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by NMR spectroscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cross peaks in PAR spectra are indicative of proximities smaller than 6–7 Å between the spins.
source: Cross peaks in PAR spectra are indicative of proximities smaller than 6–7 Å between the spins
evidence: This is based on the known properties of PAR NMR spectroscopy.

claim: No signals were observed in the NMR spectra for residues M1-V15, K21-V37 and V95-A140 in the α-Syn fibril structure.
source: Interestingly, no signals were observed in the NMR spectra for residues M1-V15, K21-V37 and V95-A140 in the α-Syn fibril structure.
evidence: This is directly observed in the NMR spectroscopy data.

claim: These regions correspond precisely to the stretches in the cryo-EM structure for which model building is not possible due to lower resolution, suggesting that these regions are indeed disordered in this polymorph.
source: These regions correspond precisely to the stretches in our cryo-EM structure for which model building is not possible due to lower resolution, suggesting that these regions are indeed disordered in this polymorph.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between NMR data and cryo-EM density quality.

claim: No NMR peak doubling was observed for residues at the filament interface, and no distinction could be made between polymorphs 2a and 2b, indicating that the structures of the monomers in the polymorphs 2a and 2b are very close to each other.
source: Also, no NMR peak doubling, although present for a subset of resonances (Gath et al., 2014a), was observed for residues at the filament interface, and no distinction could be made between polymorphs 2a and 2b, indicating that the structures of the monomers in the polymorphs 2a and 2b are very close to each other.
evidence: This is inferred from the NMR spectroscopy data.

claim: For both α-Syn polymorph 2a and 2b, differences in height within residues of a protofilament reveal a hydrophobic area composed of residues Q62 to V74 (ß4-ß5).
source: For both α-Syn polymorph 2a and 2b, differences in height within residues of a protofilament reveal a hydrophobic area (Figure 2) akin to the hydrophobic cleft described for α-Syn polymorph 1a (Guerrero-Ferreira et al., 2018). It is composed of residues Q62 to V74 (ß4-ß5) (Figure 1D and E)
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structures and atomic models.

claim: These residues correspond to a stretch of exclusively hydrophobic or polar residues, completely devoid of charged amino acids.
source: These residues correspond to a stretch of exclusively hydrophobic or polar residues, completely devoid of charged amino acids.
evidence: This is determined from the amino acid sequence and the structure.

claim: Within the NAC region, residues E61-A78 are the amyloidogenic component.
source: Consistent with these results and with the concept that the hydrophobic core is essential for assembly, is the finding by El-Agnaf et al. (1998) that, within the NAC region, residues E61-A78 are the amyloidogenic component.
evidence: This is supported by a cited research publication.

claim: Cryo-EM analysis of α-Syn fibrils prepared with E46K mutant or phosphorylated and N-terminally acetylated protein shows these also to be composed of two protofilaments and having an overall diameter of 10 nm.
source: Our structural cryo-EM analysis of α-Syn fibrils prepared with E46K mutant or phosphorylated and N-terminally acetylated protein shows these also to be composed of two protofilaments and having an overall diameter of 10 nm (Figure 3).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM data.

claim: ß-sheets in α-Syn fibrils from E46K mutant, phosphorylated or N-terminally acetylated protein are arranged forming the characteristic bent β-arch like shape, and an arrangement closely resembling that of polymorph 2a.
source: As with polymorphs 1a, 2a and 2b, ß-sheets in α-Syn fibrils from E46K mutant, phosphorylated or N-terminally acetylated protein are arranged forming the characteristic bent β-arch like shape, and an arrangement closely resembling that of polymorph 2a (Figure 3).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM reconstructions.

claim: Polymorphs 2a and 2b radically differ from the construction of polymorphs 1.
source: However, closer inspection and comparison with secondary structure elements identified in previous NMR studies on equivalent fibril preparations (Bousset et al., 2013; Gath et al., 2014a) revealed that polymorphs 2a and 2b radically differ from the construction of polymorphs 1.
evidence: This is determined by structural comparison and supported by NMR data.

claim: The new structures of polymorphs 2a and 2b show an inverted bend of the first β-arch motif compared to polymorphs 1a and 1b.
source: When compared to polymorphs 1, the new structures of polymorphs 2a and 2b show an inverted bend of the first β-arch motif, comprising mainly the black and cyan segments in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is observed by comparing the atomic models of the different polymorphs.

claim: In polymorphs 2, the β-arch is formed by an inverted amino-acid sequence compared to polymorphs 1.
source: In polymorphs 2, this β-arch is formed by an inverted amino-acid sequence: when the two motifs are superimposed, the chain runs from cyan to black in one case, in the other from black to cyan.
evidence: This is determined by structural comparison of the atomic models.

claim: This inversion profoundly changes the amino acid distribution within the arch between polymorphs 1 and 2.
source: This inversion profoundly changes the amino acid distribution within the arch between polymorphs 1 and 2.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural comparison.

claim: The interface in the new polymorphs 2a and 2b is formed by electrostatic interactions through salt-bridges between residues K45 and E57, or K45 and E46, respectively.
source: Unlike the hydrophobic interaction between protofilaments in polymorph 1a by the black segment, and in 1b by the cyan and light green segments, the interface in the new polymorphs 2a and 2b is formed by electrostatic interactions in the green segment, through salt-bridges between residues K45 and E57, or K45 and E46, respectively in 2a and 2b polymorphs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed in the atomic models of the structures.

claim: The presence of an additional ß-strand ß0 on the periphery of the fibril is a remarkable difference between polymorphs 1 and polymorphs 2.
source: Furthermore, the presence of an additional ß-strand ß0 on the periphery of the fibril (in the blue segment) is a remarkable difference between polymorphs 1 and polymorphs 2.
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures of the different polymorphs.

claim: In polymorphs 2a and 2b, residues V16-E20 form a hydrophobic steric-zipper geometry with residues S87-A91, which results in the N-terminus wrapping around the fibril and enclosing the NAC region.
source: This stretch of residues, V16-E20, forms a hydrophobic steric-zipper geometry with residues S87-A91, which are part of ß7, at the end of the amyloidogenic NAC region. In polymorphs 2a and 2b, this results in the N-terminus wrapping around the fibril and enclosing the NAC region (cyan, light green and red segments).
evidence: This is observed in the atomic models of the structures.

claim: In polymorphs 2a and 2b, the serine residue at position 87, a phosphorylation site located within the NAC region, is buried inside the interface.
source: This buries the serine residue at position 87, a phosphorylation site located within the NAC region, inside this interface.
evidence: This is observed in the atomic models of the structures.

claim: In α-Syn polymorph 1a, approximately 40 residues on both ends of the α-Syn fibril are flexible and surround the fibril with a fuzzy coat, leaving part of the NAC region (K80 to V95), including S87, exposed.
source: This is in contrast to α-Syn polymorph 1a, where approximately 40 residues on both ends of the α-Syn fibril are flexible and surround the fibril with a fuzzy coat, leaving part of the NAC region (that is, K80 to V95, red and magenta segments), including S87, exposed (Figure 1B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures of polymorphs 1a and 2.

claim: There are four different polymorphs of α-Syn fibrils known at atomic resolution, including the structures presented here.
source: Presently, there are four different polymorphs of α-Syn fibrils known at atomic resolution, including the structures presented here.
evidence: This is based on the current state of knowledge in the field, including the structures presented in this manuscript.

claim: The four polymorphs can be classified into two groups with each group having a distinct fold (folds 1 and 2) at the protofilament level.
source: They can be classified into two groups with each group having a distinct fold (folds 1 and 2) (that is, at the protofilament level).
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison of the polymorphs.

claim: Within each group there are two distinct protofilament packings or assembly polymorphisms (polymorphs a and b).
source: Within each group there are two distinct protofilament packings or assembly polymorphisms (polymorphs a and b; Figure 4).
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison of the polymorphs.

claim: All fold one structures (polymorphs 1a and 1b) were grown under buffer conditions comprising either a poly-anion or a big chaotropic negative ion.
source: All fold one structures (polymorphs 1a and 1b) were grown under buffer conditions comprising either a poly-anion (that is, phosphate with three negative charges and N3- with having locally two negative charges) or a big chaotropic negative ion (that is Br-), while polymorphs 2a and 2b of wildtype α-Syn were grown under phosphate-free conditions with the only anion being Cl- (Table 1).
evidence: This is documented in the fibril preparation conditions in Table 1.

claim: Polymorphs 2a and 2b of wildtype α-Syn were grown under phosphate-free conditions with the only anion being Cl-.
source: All fold one structures (polymorphs 1a and 1b) were grown under buffer conditions comprising either a poly-anion (that is, phosphate with three negative charges and N3- with having locally two negative charges) or a big chaotropic negative ion (that is Br-), while polymorphs 2a and 2b of wildtype α-Syn were grown under phosphate-free conditions with the only anion being Cl- (Table 1).
evidence: This is documented in the fibril preparation conditions in Table 1.

claim: Adjacent to the salt-bridge H50-E57 in polymorph 1a, there are three lysine residues at positions K43, K45 and K58 that are close in space.
source: Interestingly, there are adjacent to the salt-bridge H50-E57 three lysine residues in polymorph 1a at positions K43, K45 and K58 (the latter from the other protofilament) that are close in space.
evidence: This is observed in the structure of polymorph 1a.

claim: A density in the cryo-EM map of polymorph 1a, presumably a phosphate ion of poly-anionic nature, was observed between K43, K45 and K58 that neutralizes the repulsion of the three positive charged residues.
source: Between them, Guerrero-Ferreira et al. (2018) observed a density in the cryo-EM map, presumably a phosphate ion of poly-anionic nature that neutralizes the repulsion of the three positive charged residues (Figure 4).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM density map and cited from previous work.

claim: In the absence of a neutralizing poly-anion or Br- exerting its chaotropic property, it is unlikely that polymorph one can be obtained, indicating that in the presence of Cl- as the only anion, a distinct polymorph must be formed.
source: In the absence of a neutralizing poly-anion in this area of positively charged side chains or Br- exerting its chaotropic property, it is unlikely that polymorph one can be obtained, indicating that in the presence of Cl- as the only anion, a distinct polymorph must be formed.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and the effect of buffer conditions.

claim: The fibrils of the familial variant E46K were grown under phosphate conditions but adopt polymorph 2a fold.
source: The fibrils of the familial variant E46K (Figure 3) were also grown under phosphate conditions but adopt polymorph 2a fold.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM data for E46K fibrils.

claim: The polymorph 1a fold introduces an electrostatic repulsion between K46 and K80 in the E46K mutant, instead of the 46–80 salt-bridge stabilizing this polymorph.
source: The polymorph 1a fold we obtained for the wildtype 1–121 form, introduces an electrostatic repulsion between K46 and K80, instead of the 46–80 salt-bridge stabilizing this polymorph.
evidence: This is inferred from the structure of polymorph 1a and the effect of the E46K mutation.

claim: The structural features provide a rationale how changes corresponding to only a few kcal (or less) in the stability of polymorph 1a can lead to the protein adopting an entirely different polymorph.
source: The structural features thus provide a rationale how changes corresponding to only a few kcal (or less) in the stability of polymorph 1a (such as absence/presence of phosphate, single point mutation), can lead to the protein adopting an entirely different polymorph.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and the effects of mutations and buffer conditions.

claim: This finding highlights the postulated flat energy landscape of fibril formation and the conformational promiscuity that comes along with it.
source: This finding also highlights the postulated flat energy landscape of fibril formation and the conformational promiscuity that comes along with it.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and is consistent with theoretical understanding of amyloid formation.

claim: While the packing interfaces between polymorphs 1a and 1b are both hydrophobic, they still substantially differ.
source: While the packing interfaces between polymorphs 1a and 1b are both hydrophobic, they still substantially differ, as in polymorph 1a residues V66-A78 form the interface, and in polymorph 1b residues H50-E57 form the interface (Figure 4).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures of polymorphs 1a and 1b.

claim: In polymorph 1a residues V66-A78 form the interface, and in polymorph 1b residues H50-E57 form the interface.
source: as in polymorph 1a residues V66-A78 form the interface, and in polymorph 1b residues H50-E57 form the interface (Figure 4).
evidence: This is observed in the structures of polymorphs 1a and 1b.

claim: The difference is smaller in the case of polymorphs 2, where the protofilament interactions are of inter-protofilament salt-bridge character but are packed differently.
source: The difference is smaller in the case of polymorphs 2, where the protofilament interactions are of inter-protofilament salt-bridge character but are packed differently.
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures of polymorphs 2a and 2b.

claim: The energy differences between polymorphs 2a and 2b are very minute, but still the structures are distinct.
source: It is evident that the energy differences between the two polymorphs are therefore very minute, but still the structures are distinct.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural similarity and differences between polymorphs 2a and 2b.
